Two lessons stand out: webhook delivery has a polling backstop, and automatic entity matching links only a single unambiguous candidate. I also found a cassette-time helper that keeps recorded signed-URL expirations valid during replay without changing expiry validation.

A second vendor should inherit **the reliability contracts and test strategy**, with its own API budgets, status mappings and identity model.

**1. Rate limits belong in the job design**

Instead enforces two budgets: per API group **per connection**, plus an app-wide budget. The group check runs first so a job refused by that limit does not consume the app’s allowance. Unknown groups fall back to a budgeted `default` bucket. See the [throttle configuration](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/config/initializers/sidekiq.rb:101).

The transferable lessons are:

- Make each operation job perform at most one vendor exchange, so throttling corresponds to requests.
- Keep interactive uploads and background reconciliation in separate priority lanes.
- Honor `429 Retry-After`, including both seconds and HTTP-date formats.
- Record remaining/reset headers under the same group vocabulary used by throttling.
- Bound transient retries and fail affected uploads when retries run out.

Instead’s limits—such as five document requests/minute/connection—are vendor settings, not defaults for GruntWorx. Also, the [shared retry worker](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/operation_worker.rb:9) explicitly warns that throttled rescheduling resets retry counts: an attempt budget is not a wall-clock deadline.

**2. Webhooks need a reconciliation backstop**

**The boundary is vendor-neutral in dispatch, but still assumes an OAuth-connected, document-oriented vendor.** Some assumptions are mandatory contracts; others are optional helpers shaped by Instead.

| Area | Assumption embedded today | Where another vendor would struggle |
|---|---|---|
| **Credentials and connection state** | `Connection` supplies encrypted access/refresh tokens, expiry fields and `HasOauthConnection` states. “Usable” means the grant can be refreshed. | API keys, Basic Auth, certificates, service accounts, or OAuth grants without refresh tokens do not naturally satisfy this contract. |
| **Connecting** | Authorization starts by returning `authorization_url`; completion accepts `code` and `redirect_uri`. | Credential-entry forms, client-credentials OAuth, device authorization or asynchronous provisioning need a different connection flow. |
| **Request authentication** | Every `BaseClient#request` obtains an access token; an HTTP `401` triggers forced refresh. | A `401` caused by an invalid API key or vendor-specific authorization rule cannot be repaired that way. |
| **Disconnecting and recovery** | Disconnect retains tokens until asynchronous revocation; renewal and grant verification are shared operations. | Vendors with no token-revocation endpoint, manual credential rotation or different credential lifecycles need different semantics. |
| **Account binding** | One selected provider and one external tenant binding per firm. | Multiple vendor accounts, offices or credentials selected per client are outside that selection model. |
| **Uploads** | The shared signed-target implementation models a multipart form POST. | Raw signed PUT, required signed headers, direct API uploads and resumable uploads do not fit that helper. |
| **Capabilities** | A class-level passport describes static file extensions and an integer MB limit per return type, plus a vendor-wide year list. | Account-specific entitlements, different years per form, page limits, product options or batch limits cannot be represented directly. |
| **Submission and results** | The common record represents one source document sent under a provider, tax preparation and return type. | Job/package-oriented vendors need adapter records that translate job-level acceptance and results onto individual document records. |
| **Reconciliation** | A registered adapter must accept stale document IDs through `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync`; the sweep requires a `connected` row. | A vendor without status reads cannot implement equivalent recovery; non-OAuth connection models still face the state assumption. |

**OAuth is part of the shared substrate, not merely the Instead adapter.**  
[`BaseClient#request`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:280) always enters `with_access_token` and refreshes on unauthorized responses. [`HasOauthConnection`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:28) requires token/status columns and guards connection transitions using both access and refresh tokens. The common [connection completion service](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:17) also exposes OAuth callback parameters. API-key onboarding would require a different core entry point or fabricated OAuth-shaped behavior.

**The signed-upload abstraction is narrower than its name suggests.**  
`PresignedUploadTarget` carries `http_method`, but [`upload_to_signed_target`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/base_client.rb:243) always calls `.post` with multipart fields. Its constructor requires a nonempty `fields` hash, so a valid signed PUT URL with no form fields is rejected.

This is an optional helper: an adapter’s `ExportAsync` can own a different upload workflow. It becomes a portability problem only if treated as the universal upload port.

**Some shared export rules encode Instead’s storage behavior.**  
[`ValidateDocuments`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:79) rejects an already-uploaded, nonarchived document and permits another send after archive. Its rationale explicitly depends on Instead’s per-entity path collisions and archive behavior. A vendor supporting revisions, overwrite, or repeated jobs may need different duplicate-send rules.

**The failure vocabulary is useful, but its recovery policy is OAuth-shaped.**  
The shared [`RefusalsHelper`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/refusals_helper.rb:25) maps insufficient scope and invalid grant to `unauthorized`; reconnect resumes those uploads. The shared state machines, ownership checks, provider snapshots and common failure reasons remain useful domain contracts. The main compatibility questions are authentication, submission identity, duplicate-send semantics and capability granularity. These are source-backed limitations; whether GruntWorx actually conflicts with each one still requires its API contract. The dependency report judged no edges for this scope, so it provides no additional verdict on protocol fit.

The adapter returns a connection with `external_tenant_uuid`; the shared service compares it with `FirmSettings.external_tenant_uuid`:

**They fail visibly, then can be resumed automatically after reconnect.** They do not remain indefinitely in `waiting` or `uploading`.

When the grant is rejected, affected uploads are marked:

upload_status = failed

After a successful reconnect, the shared connection flow schedules `ResumeSendsAsync`. It selects **nondeleted documents belonging to that firm and provider** whose upload is `failed` with reason `unauthorized`, groups them by tax preparation, and passes the existing send records back to the adapter’s `ExportAsync`.

| Failure reason | Automatically resumed after reconnect? |
|---|---|
| `unauthorized` | **Yes** |
| `forbidden` — local permission denial | No |
| `network_error` — exhausted retries | No |
| `api_error` | No |
| `exceeded` | No |
| Other reasons | No |

Под **маркером привязки** я имею в виду `FirmSettings.external_tenant_uuid` — идентификатор аккаунта фирмы **на стороне провайдера**.

Он отвечает на вопрос: **«К какому внешнему аккаунту относятся уже сохранённые vendor ID и отправленные документы?»** Это не токен доступа, не идентификатор сотрудника и не `client_id` налогоплательщика.

Например:

```text
TaxDome firm: 42
provider: instead
external_tenant_uuid: account-A
```

После первого подключения TaxDome сохраняет `account-A`. При последующих подключениях проверяет, что новые credentials открывают доступ к тому же аккаунту. Иначе старые внешние идентификаторы могут перестать работать или начать адресовать чужие данные.

| Ситуация | Поведение |
|---|---|
| Привязки нет, провайдер сообщил A | Сохранить A |
| Сохранено A, провайдер сообщил A | Разрешить подключение |
| Сохранено A, провайдер сообщил B | Откатить подключение с `account_mismatch`; попытаться отозвать новый grant |
| Провайдер не сообщил идентификатор | Пропустить проверку; существующую привязку сохранить |

**Как значение попадает в settings.** Адаптер возвращает connection с атрибутом `external_tenant_uuid`. В общем OAuth concern это временный атрибут объекта; постоянное значение хранится в `FirmSettings`. У Instead источником служит `firm_uuid` из ответа token endpoint.

**Когда привязка снимается:**

- при явном отключении;
- при `Connections::DisconnectAll`;
- при переключении на другого провайдера.

Обычное истечение или отклонение grant само по себе не означает смену внешнего аккаунта — привязка нужна именно для безопасного reconnect.

Для GWX нужен **стабильный идентификатор внешнего аккаунта, в границах которого действуют идентификаторы клиентов, заданий и файлов**. Если GWX такого значения не возвращает, текущий общий механизм допускает подключение, но защитить от reconnect в другой аккаунт не сможет.

Ещё ограничение: поле одно на фирму и выбранного провайдера. Оно не моделирует несколько одновременно подключённых аккаунтов GWX. При этом несколько фирм TD могут быть привязаны к одному внешнему аккаунту.

|---|---|

| Сохранено A, провайдер сообщил A | Разрешить подключение |
| Сохранено A, провайдер сообщил B | Откатить подключение с `account_mismatch`; попытаться отозвать новый grant |
